quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is when cars turn left in front of motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: To help other drivers see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Maintain eye contact with other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Turning on your headlight is the best way to make your motorcycle visible to other drivers. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, you should usually:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest, but this can change depending on conditions.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All motorcycle riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake does not build good braking habits or skills for emergency stops.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may give poor traction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or utility covers.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material when riding to be more visible to other drivers. Always cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You can go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, do a safety check. Test your brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see the cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see the cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the paint.
questions.explanation: Before a ride, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during the day.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can use a motorized scooter.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Recommended for all rides.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The road is very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better grip.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. They connect the front and rear brakes when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.
